To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PTHr and PTHr are potent stimulators of bone resorption, that the actions of PTHrP on bone cells are mediated by initial actions on osteoblasts rather than on osteoclasts, and that the structural requirements for PTHrP to promote bone resorption are similar to those for PTHr to promote cAMP accumulation in osteoblasts.
PTHr‐related peptide (PTHrP), like parathyroid hormone (PTH), stimulates bone resorption in the isolated rat osteoclast assay only in the presence or in coculture with osteoblasts.
PTHr‐related protein is a potent stimulant of osteoclastic bone resorption, but that the resorption is mediated through actions on cells of the osteoclast lineage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which parathyroid hormone and its related protein (PTHr) act on bone to promote bone resorption.
the molecular mechanisms of bone resorption, the process whereby bone is broken down and calcium and phosphate are returned to the circulation for use in the body.
the molecular and cellular basis for the actions of parathyroid‐related protein on bone resorption.

the PTHrPs are the most potent stimulator of osteoclastic bone resorption known to date.

the PTHrPs are not only potent stimulators of osteoclastic bone resorption, but also potent stimulators of bone formation.
